Map code entry 0 (action 0): JMP screen_shake ($044C), the sound and shaking screen of a howitzer shell going off. It returns with the carry that random_byte's last addition left ($24EC), so whether the game redraws the view afterwards ($8872) is left to chance. The howitzer stands at (28,2), check square 12 (message 7, "This is a working howitzer. You don't see any shells around, though."): Using a Howitzer shell (item 33) on it leads to check square 6: IQ 5, Demolitions 4 or AT weapon 2, one conscious member passing being enough. Passed (message 67, the shell clicks into place), question square 3 offers six shots (message 87: west, southwest or south, low or high), and each answer is a class-6 square, 9-14 ($3DE3-$3DF2), that runs this routine and then becomes remote-change square 19-24, the impact (message 90, "BOOM! The shell arcs high and impacts with an explosion!"), which piles rubble on its target area (remote-change square 21, shot C, leaves craters instead: message square 14, "You walk through the crater.") and turns the party's square into class-6 square 3-8 (other_party_in_blast). Failed, class-6 square 2 ($3D34) runs this routine and becomes check square 9, which fails for any party without the skill-37 marker in the first place: everybody loses 5d6 CON (message 49, "You screw up somehow and the shell explodes!"), less an armour roll of each member's AC (+$1A) in d6 since flag bit 0 is clear ($A8B2-$A8C5), and the howitzer is left in pieces (tile square 0, message 86).

For each party from last_party ($0B) down to 0, except the current one ($08), whose table (party_table_ptr $029F, $68/$69) gives this map ($09) at +$0A, its column and row (+8/+9) are compared with each (column, row) pair of the square's record from +7 up to $FF. Returns carry clear. Class-6 squares 3-8 ($3D37, $3D47, $3D65, $3D81, $3D91, $3DBB), which impacts 19-24 leave on the party's square, run it; each lists its shot's target squares. All give message square 2 on a match (message 89, "Your other party is swamped in rubble from the explosion!"), which then leads to remote-change square 16 as a miss does at once: the howitzer square becomes check square 12 again, ready for the next shell. The routine only picks the message; nothing in it touches the other party.
